What Apple Mail Remind Me Later is — and what your listing may claim

Apple markets Remind Me Later in the Mail app as a snooze and remind-later action on a received email — buyers defer one message so Mail surfaces it again at a chosen time instead of leaving it buried in the inbox. Western indie listings often show one or more of these surfaces on the US product page. AppLocale covers paste-ready zh-Hans copy for whichever your screenshots and description already claim:

  • Remind Me Later action (稍后提醒) — gallery frames showing the Remind Me Later menu or swipe action on a message thread
  • Remind Me picker (Remind Me) — marketing that buyers pick when Mail should nudge them again — later today, tomorrow, or custom deferral
  • Follow Up Later (Follow Up Later) — when your English gallery emphasizes follow-up timing and deferred mail return workflows
  • Snooze email (邮件稍后提醒) — hero copy for per-message deferral so one thread reappears when the buyer is ready
  • Deferred mail return (稍后查看邮件) — when your en-US listing uses remind-later as the hero story for inbox follow-up and snooze productivity

Your gallery may lead with a Remind Me Later picker on one frame and a snoozed thread badge on the next. zh-Hans caption lines should name the correct surface per frame — remind-later snooze is not Mail Catch Up triage cards, not Reminders app task lists, and not Schedule Send compose pickers.
